paper_metadata.title: Effect of Al and Ti additions on the high cycle fatigue behavior of CoCrNi-based medium-entropy alloys at room and high temperatures
paper_metadata.journal: Fatigue & Fracture of Engineering Materials & Structures

evidence.quote: For the application of medium-entropy alloys (MEAs) in engineering, high cycle fatigue behavior of CoCrNi-based MEAs with different Al and Ti additions was investigated at room temperature (RT) and 350 /C14 C in this study.

The fatigue behavior of CoCrNi-based MEAs with differ-
ent Al and Ti contents at RT and high temperatures was
investigated in this study.

evidence.quote: Figure 5D,E shows the bright-field and dark-field TEM images, respectively, of AT43, which show a large number of uniformly distributed nanosized second-phase precipitates. The precipitates were the γ phase with the L1 2 (Ni, Co, Cr) 3(Ti, Al) structure.29 In this study, the average precipitate size was /C14 17 nm.

The precipitates had high concentrations of Ni, Ti, and Al and slightly low concentrations of Co and Cr. The elemental distribution in also verified the existence of L1 2 (Ni, Co, Cr)3(Ti, Al)-type particles in AT43.

evidence.quote: As shown in Figure 12A, at 350 /C14 C and under σ max = 290 MPa, AT12-14 had several dislocations, because σ max (290 MPa) was slightly larger than σy (281 MPa), and many dislocations were produced in the yield stage. evidence.quote: Microstructure analysis indicated that higher tensile and fatigue strength were attributed to uniformly distributed precipitates of nanoscale L1 2 particles formed in the FCC matrix.
Therefore, the tensile strength of NiCoCr-based MEAs can be strengthened significantly by adding Al and Ti because of the uniformly distributed precipitates of nanoscale L1 2 particles.
